ok.de: Richtig: Müdigkeit jetzt + „all afternoon“ → have been studying, die Tätigkeit mit Spur im Jetzt.
ok.en: Right: tired now + “all afternoon” → have been studying, an activity with a trace in the present.

wrong.de: Grammatisch möglich, doch gesucht ist die Dauerform: have been studying.
wrong.en: Grammatically possible, but the continuous form is wanted: have been studying.

wrong.de: Past Simple blickt auf Vergangenes zurück; hier wirkt die Tätigkeit bis jetzt nach.
wrong.en: Past Simple looks back at the past; here the activity still shows in the present.

wrong.de: am studying beschreibt nur den Moment, nicht den ganzen Nachmittag bis jetzt.
wrong.en: am studying describes only this moment, not the whole afternoon up to now.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have been + studying.
wrong.en: been is missing: have been + studying.

ok.de: „How long“ + Dauer bis jetzt → have you been learning, nicht das Präsens des Deutschen.
ok.en: “How long” + duration up to now → have you been learning, not the German-style present.

wrong.de: Present Simple fragt nach Gewohnheit, nicht nach der Dauer bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Simple asks about habit, not about duration up to now.

wrong.de: Present Continuous gilt für jetzt, nicht für den Zeitraum bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Continuous covers now, not the period up to now.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossene Zeit, du lernst aber noch.
wrong.en: Past Simple means finished time, but you are still learning.

ok.de: „since 2019“ + Dauer bis heute → has been living oder has lived. Beides stimmt.
ok.en: “since 2019” + duration until today → has been living or has lived. Both are right.

wrong.de: Present Simple passt nicht zu since: Dauer bis jetzt braucht has lived / has been living.
wrong.en: Present Simple does not go with since: duration up to now needs has lived / has been living.

wrong.de: Present Continuous zeigt nur jetzt; since 2019 verlangt die Zeit bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Continuous shows only now; since 2019 needs the time up to now.

wrong.de: Past Simple wäre abgeschlossen, sie wohnt aber noch hier: has lived.
wrong.en: Past Simple would be finished, but she still lives here: has lived.

wrong.de: Nach has braucht es lived oder been living.
wrong.en: After has you need lived or been living.

ok.de: „since 8:15“ + die Suche läuft noch → have been looking.
ok.en: “since 8:15” + the search is still going → have been looking.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossene Zeit; du suchst aber noch.
wrong.en: Past Simple means finished time, but you are still looking.

wrong.de: Present Continuous passt nicht zu since: Es fehlt der Blick zurück.
wrong.en: Present Continuous does not go with since: the look back is missing.

wrong.de: Present Simple nennt eine Gewohnheit, hier läuft eine Suche seit 8:15.
wrong.en: Present Simple names a habit; here a search has been running since 8:15.

ok.de: know ist ein Zustandsverb, also ohne -ing: How long have you known our CFO?
ok.en: know is a state verb, so no -ing: How long have you known our CFO?

wrong.de: know steht nie in der -ing-Form, auch nicht im Present Continuous.
wrong.en: know never takes the -ing form, not even in the Present Continuous.

wrong.de: Present Simple passt nicht zu „How long“ + Zeitraum bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Simple does not go with “How long” + a period up to now.

wrong.de: Die Dauerform geht bei know nicht, es ist ein Zustandsverb.
wrong.en: The continuous form does not work with know; it is a state verb.

ok.de: „since January“ + die Arbeit läuft noch → has been working.
ok.en: “since January” + the work is still going → has been working.

wrong.de: Present Simple passt nicht zu since: Dauer bis jetzt braucht has been working.
wrong.en: Present Simple does not go with since: duration up to now needs has been working.

wrong.de: Present Continuous zeigt nur jetzt, nicht die Zeit seit Januar.
wrong.en: Present Continuous shows only now, not the time since January.

wrong.de: Past Simple wäre abgeschlossen, aber die Arbeit geht weiter.
wrong.en: Past Simple would be finished, but the work goes on.

ok.de: two years ist eine Zeitspanne → for. since braucht einen Zeitpunkt (since 2022).
ok.en: two years is a length of time → for. since needs a point in time (since 2022).

wrong.de: ago steht mit Past Simple und stünde nach „two years“, nicht davor.
wrong.en: ago goes with the Past Simple and would follow “two years”, not precede it.

wrong.de: since braucht einen Startpunkt wie 2022; two years nennt eine Länge.
wrong.en: since needs a starting point like 2022; two years names a length.

wrong.de: from braucht ein Gegenstück (from … to …); für die Dauer steht for.
wrong.en: from needs a counterpart (from … to …); for a duration use for.

ok.de: „since Tuesday“ + Handlung bis jetzt → Have you been waiting.
ok.en: “since Tuesday” + an action up to now → Have you been waiting.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossene Zeit; das Warten dauert aber an.
wrong.en: Past Simple means finished time, but the waiting continues.

wrong.de: Present Simple passt nicht zu since: So klingt „Wartest du seit Dienstag?“ wörtlich.
wrong.en: Present Simple does not go with since: it is the word-for-word German version.

wrong.de: Present Continuous passt nicht zu since: Es fehlt der Blick zurück.
wrong.en: Present Continuous does not go with since: the look back is missing.

ok.de: „since 6 p.m.“ + die Musik läuft noch → have been playing.
ok.en: “since 6 p.m.” + the music is still on → have been playing.

wrong.de: Present Continuous zeigt nur jetzt, nicht die Zeit seit 6 Uhr.
wrong.en: Present Continuous shows only now, not the time since 6 p.m.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossen; die Musik läuft aber noch.
wrong.en: Past Simple means finished, but the music is still on.

wrong.de: Present Simple nennt eine Gewohnheit und passt nicht zu since.
wrong.en: Present Simple names a habit and does not go with since.

ok.de: „since 2017“ → Dauer bis jetzt → have been working. have worked geht auch.
ok.en: “since 2017” → duration up to now → have been working. have worked also works.

wrong.de: Present Simple passt nicht zu since: Dauer bis jetzt braucht have been working.
wrong.en: Present Simple does not go with since: duration up to now needs have been working.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossene Zeit; ihr arbeitet aber noch zusammen.
wrong.en: Past Simple means finished time, but you still work together.

wrong.de: Present Continuous zeigt nur jetzt; since 2017 braucht den Blick zurück.
wrong.en: Present Continuous shows only now; since 2017 needs the look back.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have been working.
wrong.en: been is missing: have been working.

ok.de: „all day“ betont die Dauer bis jetzt → have been trying. have tried geht auch.
ok.en: “all day” stresses the duration up to now → have been trying. have tried also works.

wrong.de: Present Simple nennt eine Gewohnheit; „all day“ meint die Zeit bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Simple names a habit; “all day” means the time up to now.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossene Zeit; du versuchst es aber weiter.
wrong.en: Past Simple means finished time, but you keep trying.

wrong.de: Present Continuous zeigt nur jetzt, nicht den ganzen Tag bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Continuous shows only now, not the whole day up to now.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have been trying.
wrong.en: been is missing: have been trying.

ok.de: Spur im Jetzt (schmutzige Hände) + „all morning“ → have been working. have worked geht auch.
ok.en: Trace in the present (dirty hands) + “all morning” → have been working. have worked also works.

wrong.de: Past Simple wäre möglich, gesucht ist hier die Perfect-Form mit Spur im Jetzt.
wrong.en: Past Simple is possible, but the Perfect form with a trace in the present is wanted.

wrong.de: Present Simple nennt eine Gewohnheit, hier geht es um den Morgen bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Simple names a habit; here it is about the morning up to now.

wrong.de: Present Continuous zeigt nur jetzt, nicht den ganzen Morgen.
wrong.en: Present Continuous shows only now, not the whole morning.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have been working.
wrong.en: been is missing: have been working.

ok.de: „lately“ + Entwicklung bis jetzt → haven't been making. haven't made geht auch.
ok.en: “lately” + a development up to now → haven't been making. haven't made also works.

wrong.de: Present Continuous passt nicht zu lately: gemeint ist die Zeit bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Continuous does not go with lately: the period up to now is meant.

wrong.de: Present Simple nennt eine Gewohnheit; lately blickt auf die letzte Zeit zurück.
wrong.en: Present Simple names a habit; lately looks back at recent time.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossene Zeit; lately reicht bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Past Simple means finished time; lately reaches up to now.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have not been making.
wrong.en: been is missing: have not been making.

ok.de: „for months“ + die Suche läuft noch → has been looking. has looked geht auch.
ok.en: “for months” + the search is still going → has been looking. has looked also works.

wrong.de: Present Simple nennt eine Gewohnheit; „for months“ meint die Zeit bis jetzt.
wrong.en: Present Simple names a habit; “for months” means the time up to now.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossene Zeit; die Suche geht aber weiter.

wrong.de: Present Continuous zeigt nur jetzt, nicht die Monate bis jetzt.

wrong.en: been is missing: has been looking.

ok.de: Beginn früher + noch im Gange + „since 9 a.m.“ → have been working. have worked geht auch.
ok.en: Earlier start + still going + “since 9 a.m.” → have been working. have worked also works.

wrong.de: Present Simple passt nicht zu since: Dauer bis jetzt braucht have been working.
wrong.en: Present Simple does not go with since: duration up to now needs have been working.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossene Zeit; sie arbeiten aber noch daran.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have been working.
wrong.en: been is missing: have been working.

ok.de: „since 3 p.m.“ + der Regen dauert an → has been raining.
ok.en: “since 3 p.m.” + the rain is continuing → has been raining.

wrong.de: Present Simple nennt eine Regel; since 3 p.m. braucht den Blick zurück.
wrong.en: Present Simple states a rule; since 3 p.m. needs the look back.

wrong.de: Present Continuous zeigt nur jetzt, nicht die Zeit seit 15 Uhr.
wrong.en: Present Continuous shows only now, not the time since 3 p.m.

wrong.de: Past Simple meint abgeschlossen; es regnet aber noch.
wrong.en: Past Simple means finished, but it is still raining.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: has been raining.
wrong.en: been is missing: has been raining.

ok.de: „since Monday“ verlangt Perfect, nicht Present Continuous: have been waiting.
ok.en: “since Monday” needs the Perfect, not the Present Continuous: have been waiting.

wrong.de: Present Continuous passt nicht zu since: Dauer bis jetzt → have been waiting.
wrong.en: Present Continuous does not go with since: duration up to now → have been waiting.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have been waiting.
wrong.en: been is missing: have been waiting.

wrong.de: since Monday nennt den Startpunkt und soll stehen bleiben.
wrong.en: since Monday names the starting point and should stay.

ok.en: “How long” + duration up to now → have you been working (or have you worked).

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: How long have you been working.
wrong.en: been is missing: How long have you been working.

ok.de: Bei he/she/it steht has: He has been feeling tired.
ok.en: he/she/it takes has: He has been feeling tired.

wrong.de: Bei he/she/it heißt es has, auch mitten in der langen Form.
wrong.en: With he/she/it use has, even inside the long form.

wrong.de: Nach been steht die -ing-Form: feeling, nicht die Grundform.
wrong.en: After been use the -ing form: feeling, not the base form.

wrong.de: Nach been steht die -ing-Form: feeling, nicht das Partizip.
wrong.en: After been use the -ing form: feeling, not the participle.

wrong.de: Die Form braucht been: has been feeling.
wrong.en: The form needs been: has been feeling.

ok.de: Zwei Fehler: Present Continuous mit since, und eine Zeitspanne braucht for: have been waiting for.
ok.en: Two errors: Present Continuous with since, and a length of time needs for: have been waiting for.

wrong.de: Zwei Fehler: Present Continuous, und 20 minutes ist eine Spanne, also for.
wrong.en: Two errors: Present Continuous, and 20 minutes is a length, so for.

wrong.de: 20 minutes ist eine Zeitspanne, deshalb for. since braucht einen Zeitpunkt.
wrong.en: 20 minutes is a length of time, so for. since needs a point in time.

wrong.en: been is missing: have been waiting for 20 minutes.

ok.en: After been comes the -ing form: have been studying.
